en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Maidens (Kumāribhūtavagga) 82.
The Training Rule for Every Year.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were ordaining [novices] every year, and the residence did not suffice.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs ordain every year? The residence does not suffice!"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, criticizing, and complaining.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [and so forth]... they grumbled, criticized, and complained, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs give the full admission every year?"... [and so forth].
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs are ordaining [them] every year?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunīs ordain every year?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: [The rule follows]"
“Whatever nun, however, should ordain [a girl] every year, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the type of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Every year" (anuvassaṃ):
"Yearly. "One should ordain" means one should confer full admission.
If she seeks out a group, a preceptor, a bowl, or a robe, thinking, “I will give the full admission,” or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the motion (ñatti), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
For each of the two formal proclamations (kammavācā), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation (*kammavācā*), there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for the preceptor;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) for the community and for the teacher.
There is no offense—
If she ordains one [nun] at intervals,
or if she is insane,
or if she is a first-offender.
The twelfth training rule is finished.
